subject: Post-call: target cost buckets and competitive comparison vs hosts
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Emma Cole <emma@finvantage.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: target cost buckets + benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Hi Emma — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the asks we agreed on so we can move toward procurement. I captured the key points below and included next steps.

Summary of what you shared
- Monthly active inference: initial pilot ~150M tokens/mo, scale target 450–600M tokens/mo in 3–6 months.
- Latency requirement: ~ <400ms p95 for chat workflows; occasional batch jobs for async summarization.
- Quality bar: current eval set needs >92% intent/safety pass rate.
- Budget posture: finance gave a ballpark committed budget of $40k–$60k/mo for production; procurement asked us for a target $/1M token rate to compare against incumbent hosts.

Camila's suggested cost buckets (we can firm these with an internal price review)
- Tier A (pilot): 150–250M tokens/mo — target $/1M = $16–$20 (short-term, higher overhead for smaller pools)
- Tier B (growth): 250–500M tokens/mo — target $/1M = $10–$14 (reserved capacity + modest commit)
- Tier C (scale): 500M+ tokens/mo — target $/1M = $6–$9 (deep commit + quantization/optimizations)

Benchmark note (high-level):
- OpenAI/Anthropic (public comparables): commonly quoted in our fieldwork at mid-teens per 1M tokens for chat-heavy workloads if you need latest safety models; Anthropic sometimes slightly lower depending on model choice.
- Open-model hosts (self-hosting/open-host services): big variance — cheaper at scale if you can accept quantized variants and slightly higher latency; ranges we see $5–$12/1M depending on architecture and GPU share.

Attachments: I attached an initial cost model workbook that converts your monthly token ranges into total monthly spend across different tiering/commit assumptions (redwood-initial-cost-model.xlsx). Also attached a short scope summary (finvantage-scope-summary.pdf).

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the 450–600M tokens/mo scale target is the committee target for Q4? If not, give a more precise midpoint we should model.
2) Procurement asked whether Redwood can do a draft SOW + standard enterprise T&Cs and a preliminary rate card for Tier B and Tier C — should I put those in a DocuSign-ready packet?
3) If acceptable, we’ll model two price ladders: (A) short-term promotional credit for first 2 months (applied to pilot), (B) commit-based ladder to hit $6–$9/1M at 500M+.

Happy to jump on a follow-up with procurement next week; propose Tue 08/24 or Wed 08/25.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Emma Cole <emma@finvantage.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: target cost buckets + benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Thanks Camila — this is super helpful and aligned with our notes. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Volume: the 450–600M tokens/mo is our internal stretch target for Q4; our procurement baseline for negotiations will be modeled on ~500M tokens/mo.
2) Budget: finance is comfortable modeling up to $50k/mo committed for a first-year deal, but preference is to keep unit economics near $8–$12/1M tokens if possible once we hit 400–500M.
3) Competitors: procurement has a memo that lists OpenAI and Anthropic as first comparables; they also asked to see pricing from open-host providers (replicate/hf stones) for a like-for-like quantized variant.

Can you do two things: (A) run the attached workbook against a 500M tokens/mo baseline and show the delta to $8/1M vs $12/1M and (B) confirm what Redwood would require (commit term, SLA) to reach $8/1M at 500M.

We are happy to take the draft SOW + T&Cs — please put the packet into DocuSign when ready and cc procurement (procurement@finvantage.com).

Appreciate the fast follow-up — Emma
Emma Cole
Head of Product, FinVantage
emma@finvantage.com

Subject: RE: Post-call recap: target cost buckets + benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Looping in Rishi to confirm commercial levers we can use. Quick internal note for the packet we will send:

- To hit the lower bound ($8/1M at 500M) we will likely need a 12–18 month committed reservation with a 30–40% prepaid portion or Minimum Commitment Level to justify dedicated pools and deeper packing (this reduces overhead and allows quantized variants in the tail).
- Alternative (lower friction): a 6–12 month commit with a blended ladder that starts at ~$12/1M and drops to ~$8/1M once the 500M threshold is hit for two consecutive months.
- We should push optional add-ons: extended observability retention, audit logs, and dedicated on-call support (those are common procurement asks and justify margin).

Rishi — can you (1) populate the rate-card lines (Pilot / Growth / Scale) into the workbook and (2) draft a short comment for procurement that explains typical SLA/credit terms tied to latency SLOs? I’ll assemble the DocuSign packet and proposed SOW.

Thanks — Marissa

- Draft SOW (scope + initial pilot milestones)
- Rate card for Pilot/Growth/Scale with the two ladder options we discussed (6–12mo blended ladder and 12–18mo deep commit)

We note FinVantage preference for a target of $8–$10/1M once 500M sustained usage is reached. Please include an appendix that summarizes how Redwood’s pricing compares to OpenAI/Anthropic and a short paragraph on what tradeoffs (latency, model freshness, KV caching) lead to the delta vs open-host pricing.

Procurement is ready to review the DocuSign packet next week. Please cc procurement@finvantage.com when the packet is ready.
